reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Reporting the combined grade without the Spetzler-Martin grade used.
name: Lawton-Young Supplementary AVM Grade

version.label: Lawton-Young supplementary grading scale (Lawton et al. 2010)
version.detail: Age (<20 years 1, 20–40 years 2, >40 years 3) + unruptured presentation (1; ruptured 0) + diffuse nidus (1; compact 0): supplementary grade 1–5. Adding the Spetzler-Martin grade gives the combined Supp-SM grade (2–10).

purpose: Adds patient and AVM features to the Spetzler-Martin grade to refine surgical risk estimation.
intendedPopulation: Patients with brain AVMs being considered for microsurgical resection.

calculatorNotice.title: Use with the Spetzler-Martin grade
calculatorNotice.message: Enter the Spetzler-Martin grade to see the combined Supp-SM grade. Neither grade is a treatment decision.

options.label: Diffuse
options.detail: Poorly defined nidus with intervening brain.

calculationMethod.share: Lawton-Young supplementary grade {total}{combined > 0 ? '; Spetzler-Martin ' + roman(sm) + '; Supp-SM ' + combined : ''}

resultStates.label: Supplementary grade {total}
resultStates.detail: Add the Spetzler-Martin grade for the combined Supp-SM grade (2–10).

resultStates.label: Supp-SM grade {combined}
resultStates.detail: In the derivation and validation cohorts, higher Supp-SM grades were associated with a higher risk of worse neurological outcome after resection.

clinicalContext.text: Supplements the Spetzler-Martin grade with age, rupture status and nidus diffuseness.
The combined Supp-SM grade predicted surgical outcome better than Spetzler-Martin alone in the derivation and validation series.

clinicalInsights.text: Ruptured presentation scores 0: patients presenting with haemorrhage often already have a deficit, which lowers the additional risk attributed to surgery.
Report the supplementary grade, the Spetzler-Martin grade and the combined grade together.

limitations.text: Derived and validated in surgical series; not designed for radiosurgery or embolisation decisions.

limitations: Group-level association with outcome; not an individual prediction.

confounders.effect: Obscures the nidus and its compactness.

whatItDoesNotTellYou: The natural history or haemorrhage risk.

guideSections.what: A 1–5 supplementary grade from age, rupture status and nidus diffuseness, added to the Spetzler-Martin grade for a combined 2–10 grade.
guideSections.whenToUse: Refining surgical risk estimation for brain AVMs alongside the Spetzler-Martin grade.
guideSections.howToPerform: Score age, presentation and nidus pattern, and sum. Add the Spetzler-Martin grade for the combined Supp-SM grade.
guideSections.clinicalContext: An input to multidisciplinary decisions with the patient's presentation and preferences.

sources.citation: Lawton MT, Kim H, McCulloch CE, Mikhak B, Young WL. A supplementary grading scale for selecting patients with brain arteriovenous malformations for surgery. Neurosurgery. 2010;66(4):702-713.

Kim H, Abla AA, Nelson J, et al. Validation of the supplemented Spetzler-Martin grading system for brain arteriovenous malformations in a multicenter cohort of 1009 surgical patients. Neurosurgery. 2015;76(1):25-31.
